name: Battle of Shiloh
description: The Battle of Shiloh was fought April 6-7, 1862, at Pittsburg Landing on the Tennessee River in Hardin County, Tennessee. Confederate forces under Albert Sidney Johnston attacked Grant's Army of the Tennessee on April 6 and pushed it back toward the river. Johnston was killed that afternoon and Beauregard took command. Buell's Army of the Ohio and Lew Wallace's division arrived that night. Grant counterattacked on April 7, and Beauregard withdrew toward Corinth.
significance: With about 23,700 casualties it was the bloodiest battle of the war to that point. It ended Confederate hopes of stopping the Union advance into Mississippi, and Union forces occupied Corinth on May 30.

timeline.label: April 6, 5:00 AM
timeline.title: Pickets clash at Fraley Field
timeline.description: Five of Grant's six divisions are camped between Shiloh Church and the Tennessee River, with no entrenchments. Confederate pickets fire on a Union patrol near Fraley Field. Lew Wallace's division is at Crump's Landing, downriver. All Union camp positions are estimates from the narrative.

events.title: Skirmish near Fraley Field
events.description: About 5:00 AM Confederate pickets fire on a patrol sent out by Col. Everett Peabody without Prentiss's knowledge. The skirmish lasts over an hour. At about 5:30 AM Johnston orders a general attack.

timeline.label: April 6, 7:30 AM
timeline.title: The Confederate line deploys
timeline.description: The Confederates lose about an hour getting ready and another hour skirmishing at Seay Field. Sherman rides out near Rea Field around 7:00 AM and is slightly wounded, which convinces him he is under attack. Beauregard orders Polk's and Breckinridge's corps forward to the flanks. Confederate positions are estimates.

events.title: Sherman is fired on near Rea Field
events.description: Sherman is slightly wounded and an orderly is killed, which convinces him the army is under attack.

events.title: Polk and Breckinridge ordered to the flanks
events.description: Beauregard sends the corps of Polk and Breckinridge forward on the flanks, which thins and extends the Confederate line.

events.title: Hurlbut sends Veatch to help Sherman
events.description: At 8:00 AM Hurlbut has his three brigades ready and sends Veatch's brigade to support Sherman.

timeline.label: April 6, 9:00 AM
timeline.title: Prentiss's camp falls; Grant arrives
timeline.description: By 8:30 AM Peabody's brigade is pushed north and the Confederates occupy his camp. About 9:00 AM they capture Prentiss's camp, and looting slows their pursuit. Grant reaches Pittsburg Landing at about 9:00 AM and orders Lew Wallace forward and Nelson's division over the river. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Gladden mortally wounded
events.description: Brig. Gen. Adley Gladden of Withers's division is mortally wounded at about 8:45 AM.

events.title: Prentiss's camp captured
events.description: The Confederates take Prentiss's camp. Looting slows their pursuit.

events.title: Grant reaches Pittsburg Landing
events.description: Grant arrives about 9:00 AM after hearing the guns from Savannah. He orders Lew Wallace to Pittsburg Landing and Nelson's division to ferry across.

timeline.label: April 6, 10:00 AM
timeline.title: Sherman falls back; the Sunken Road line forms
timeline.description: Shortly after 10:00 AM Sherman's remnants form a new line near the Hamburg-Purdy and Corinth road crossroads. Between 9:30 and 10:30 AM artillery fire is exchanged along the Sunken Road, where Prentiss and W.H.L. Wallace hold. Around 9:40 AM Stuart's brigade on the Union left is shelled and about 20 minutes later attacked. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Stuart's brigade attacked
events.description: Stuart's brigade on the Union far left receives artillery fire at about 9:40 AM. Confederate infantry attacks about 20 minutes later.

events.title: Sherman forms a new line
events.description: Sherman's remnants form near the Hamburg-Purdy and Pittsburg-Corinth crossroads.

timeline.label: April 6, 11:30 AM
timeline.title: Sherman and McClernand pushed back
timeline.description: At 11:00 AM the Confederates attack Sherman and McClernand again. By about 11:20 AM they control the Hamburg-Purdy Road and the Union line falls back. Sherman's First Brigade rejoins McClernand. Lew Wallace receives Grant's order about 11:30 AM. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Confederates control the Hamburg-Purdy Road
events.description: By 11:20 AM Sherman and McClernand fall back about 200 yards.

events.title: Lew Wallace receives Grant's message
events.description: Lew Wallace gets Grant's order about 11:30 AM and begins moving his division around noon.

timeline.label: April 6, 2:00 PM
timeline.title: Fighting at the Peach Orchard and Hornets' Nest
timeline.description: Around 2:00 PM Breckinridge attacks McArthur's partial brigade on the Union left, and Statham's brigade attacks Hurlbut's line. Prentiss and W.H.L. Wallace still hold the Sunken Road position. About 1:00 PM a Confederate bayonet charge had pushed McClernand and McDowell back to Jones Field. Lew Wallace is told he is on the wrong road. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Bayonet charge at Jones Field
events.description: A Confederate bayonet charge about 1:00 PM pushes McClernand and McDowell back to Jones Field.

events.title: Lew Wallace told he is on the wrong road
events.description: Lew Wallace receives a message at about 2:00 PM saying he is on the wrong road.

events.title: Statham attacks Hurlbut
events.description: Statham's brigade attacks Hurlbut's line while Breckinridge attacks McArthur on the Union left.

timeline.label: April 6, 2:30 PM
timeline.title: Johnston is killed
timeline.description: Albert Sidney Johnston dies at about 2:30 PM from a torn popliteal artery, about 100 yards south of the Bell Farm. Beauregard takes command. Stuart's brigade withdraws about 2:15-2:30 PM and is done fighting for the day. The location of Johnston's death is placed from the Bell Farm and is approximate.

events.title: Johnston dies on the Confederate right
events.description: Johnston bleeds to death from a torn popliteal artery. Beauregard assumes command.

events.title: Stuart's brigade withdraws
events.description: Stuart's brigade pulls back about 2:15-2:30 PM and does no more fighting that day.

timeline.label: April 6, 3:00 PM
timeline.title: Union left falls back; gunboats open fire
timeline.description: At 2:50 PM USS Tyler (Lt. William Gwin) fires on Confederate batteries near the Union left, and USS Lexington joins about an hour later. McArthur and Hurlbut fall back between 3:00 and 4:00 PM. Around 3:00 PM Grant visits Sherman and finds the Union right in poor condition. At 3:30 PM the Confederates start massing artillery against the Hornets' Nest. Positions are estimates.

events.title: USS Tyler opens fire
events.description: Lt. William Gwin's USS Tyler fires on Confederate batteries near the Union left. USS Lexington joins about an hour later.

events.title: Confederates mass artillery
events.description: The Confederates begin moving guns toward the Hornets' Nest. The battery grows to over 50 guns.

timeline.label: April 6, 4:30 PM
timeline.title: The Hornets' Nest is surrounded
timeline.description: At 4:00 PM Confederate artillery fires on Wallace and Prentiss in the Hornets' Nest, and by 4:30 PM all batteries are engaged. W.H.L. Wallace is mortally wounded about 4:15 PM while leading his division north. By 4:45 PM most of his division is off the field and Prentiss has about 2,000 men. Sherman and McClernand fall back further about 5:00 PM. Positions are estimates.

events.title: W.H.L. Wallace mortally wounded
events.description: Brig. Gen. W.H.L. Wallace is mortally wounded while leading his division north.

events.title: Artillery bombards the Hornets' Nest
events.description: Confederate guns fire on Wallace and Prentiss. All batteries are engaged by 4:30 PM.

timeline.label: April 6, 5:30 PM
timeline.title: Prentiss surrenders
timeline.description: About 5:30 PM Prentiss and several regiments surrender, with about 2,200 Union soldiers captured. Nelson's division of Buell's army begins arriving at Pittsburg Landing about 5:00 PM. At 5:35 PM USS Tyler begins hitting Chalmers's brigade directly. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Prentiss surrenders
events.description: Prentiss and several regiments surrender. About 2,200 Union soldiers are captured.

events.title: Nelson's division reaches Pittsburg Landing
events.description: The first units of Buell's army arrive about 5:00 PM.

events.title: USS Tyler hits Chalmers's brigade
events.description: The gunboat fires directly on Chalmers's brigade as it advances near Dill Branch.

timeline.label: April 6, 6:00 PM
timeline.title: The last line at Pittsburg Landing
timeline.description: Shortly after 6:00 PM Beauregard calls off all attacks. The Union holds a final line near Pittsburg Landing with massed artillery and the gunboats Tyler and Lexington firing from the river. During the final assault Lexington fires 32 rounds in 10 minutes. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Beauregard calls off the attacks
events.description: Shortly after 6:00 PM Beauregard halts the Confederate attacks. Lexington fires 32 rounds in 10 minutes during the last assault.

timeline.label: April 6, 7:15 PM
timeline.title: Lew Wallace arrives; Buell's troops reach the landing
timeline.description: About 5,800 fresh troops of Lew Wallace's division arrive about 7:15 PM and form beside Sherman. Crittenden's division begins arriving about 9:00 PM, and the whole division is at the landing two hours later. Rain begins about 10:00 PM. Gunboats shell the Confederate lines through the night. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Lew Wallace's division arrives
events.description: About 5,800 fresh troops arrive and take position beside Sherman.

events.title: Crittenden's division arrives
events.description: The first of Crittenden's division lands about 9:00 PM. The whole division is at the landing two hours later.

events.title: Grant: Lick 'em tomorrow
events.description: At midnight Sherman finds Grant resting under a tree. Grant replies, Lick 'em tomorrow, though.

timeline.label: April 7, 5:00 AM
timeline.title: Buell's attack begins
timeline.description: McCook's division reaches Savannah between midnight and 4:00 AM, and its first unit comes ashore at Pittsburg Landing about 4:00 AM. At 5:00 AM Buell's attack begins with Nelson's three brigades on the east side. A few hours later Crittenden joins Nelson on his right. Positions are estimates.

events.title: First of McCook's troops land
events.description: The first unit of McCook's division lands at Pittsburg Landing about 4:00 AM.

events.title: Nelson attacks
events.description: Buell's attack begins with Nelson's three brigades. The 47th Tennessee, the only Confederate reinforcement, arrives about 8:00 AM.

timeline.label: April 7, 10:30 AM
timeline.title: Grant's counterattack
timeline.description: Grant's attack begins about 10:30 AM with all four of his divisions advancing. Cleburne's brigade takes heavy losses in an unsuccessful assault. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Grant's attack begins
events.description: All four of Grant's divisions advance. Cleburne's brigade suffers heavy losses in an unsuccessful assault.

timeline.label: April 7, noon
timeline.title: Hornets' Nest retaken; Cheatham counterattacks
timeline.description: About noon both sides briefly withdraw from the Davis Wheat Field area and Buell's army controls the Hornets' Nest. Cheatham's division attacks Sherman and McClernand and drives them about 300 yards north. Shortly after noon Buell attacks again. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Buell's army controls the Hornets' Nest
events.description: The Hornets' Nest area is back in Union hands about noon.

events.title: Cheatham drives Sherman and McClernand back
events.description: Cheatham's division attacks and pushes Sherman and McClernand about 300 yards north.

timeline.label: April 7, 1:30 PM
timeline.title: McCook advances; fight near Water Oaks Pond
timeline.description: About 1:30 PM McCook advances west, putting Bragg's army in front of Lew Wallace, Sherman and McClernand, with McCook on its flank. Lew Wallace resumes the offensive once Sherman and McClernand push back Cheatham. After Bragg falls back south of the Hamburg-Purdy Road, Beauregard counterattacks mostly with Wood's brigade, and McCook repels it near Water Oaks Pond. Union troops cross the Hamburg-Purdy Road about 2:30 PM. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Counterattack near Water Oaks Pond
events.description: Beauregard counterattacks with a force mostly of Wood's brigade. McCook regroups near Water Oaks Pond and repels it.

events.title: Union crosses the Hamburg-Purdy Road
events.description: Union troops cross the Hamburg-Purdy Road about 2:30 PM.

timeline.label: April 7, 3:00 PM
timeline.title: Beauregard retreats toward Corinth
timeline.description: Beauregard began preparing to withdraw about 1:00 PM after learning Van Dorn was too far away. About 2:00 PM Breckinridge forms a rear guard near Shiloh Church while batteries there bombard to hide the retreat. The last Confederate artillery leaves about 3:30 PM. Grant and Buell do not pursue. Positions are estimates.

events.title: Breckinridge forms a rear guard
events.description: Breckinridge's corps forms near Shiloh Church. Batteries bombard to make the Union think the army is still there.

events.title: Retreat toward Corinth
events.description: Beauregard withdraws toward Corinth. The last Confederate artillery leaves about 3:30 PM.
